text:
leo: kicking off a quiet-burn run for redwood-instruct-3b:nf4-int4 shadowing live US-east traffic at 0.1% for 24h. main ask: slice-level regressions (hallucination/precision). auto-fallback if any high-impact slice exceeds delta>0.8% with p<0.05 within first 1k matched sessions. tagging ops — @anita @sam.

ml-onboard-bot: quiet-burn started 2208765432 — config: sample_rate=0.001, compare_to=redwood-instruct-3b:fp16, slices=['finance','legal','long_prompt>1024','code_gen'], evals=[synthetic,prod-shadow], window=1000, timeout=60s

anita: will run paired comparisons on the same requests, use bootstrap CI so we don't treat nonpaired as paired.

sam: for small n slices prefer Wilson score or bootstrap; also propose hysteresis: require 3 consecutive windows >threshold to avoid flapping.

devon: expected perf delta: +8-12ms token latency, cost savings ~-32%. will watch infra saturation.

maria: small-sample noise is real — suggest min_n=200 per slice before triggering any automated rollback. also capture examples for human review.

ml-onboard-bot: first window (1k matched sessions) complete:

```
slice: finance | n=214 | hallucin_delta=0.76% | p=0.12
slice: legal   | n=98  | hallucin_delta=1.8%  | p=0.02
slice: long_prompt>1024 | n=312 | hallucin_delta=0.22% | p=0.45
slice: code_gen | n=157 | hallucin_delta=0.95% | p=0.04
overall | n=1800 | hallucin_delta=0.35% | p=0.09
``` 
anita: legal slice p=0.02 looks concerning but n=98 < maria.min_n(200) so we shouldn't auto-fallback yet. flag for manual review.

sam: code_gen is tricky — n=157, p=0.04, delta=0.95% >0.8%. if we keep min_n=200 it won't trigger; if we set min_n lower it would. propose compromise: min_n=150 for code_gen only (higher impact on quality), keep 200 for legal/finance. also change hysteresis to 2 consecutive windows instead of 3 to catch fast regressions.

devon: agree on slice-specific min_n. operationally fallback should be: immediately route traffic for that customer-affected slice to fp16 variant in same AZ, open alert to #oncall, and create rollback ticket automatically.

maria: we also need human-in-loop examples to triage — store up to 50 failing examples per slice (masked), and flag them in the ticket.

leo: proposed consolidated rule: rollout.policy.quiet_burn.min_n = {'finance':200,'legal':200,'code_gen':150,'default':200}; rollout.policy.quiet_burn.hysteresis = 2 consecutive windows; rollback.criteria = delta>0.8% AND p<0.05 AND slice in high-impact list. fallback.target = same-model:fp16 in AZ. threshold applies to matched-window size=1000. If triggered, auto-fallback + alert + ticket.

sam: add metric capture: numerator/denominator for hallucination (human-labeled or eval classifier scores), and record sample variance so we can compute effect size. use paired-per-request difference when available.

anita: also schedule a 6h checkpoint: if no automated triggers and aggregated hallucin_delta <0.5% and latency increase <15ms, promote to 0.5% traffic. annotate promotion as manual step in the runbook.

devon: infra note: make sure KV-cache warming is identical between variants during shadow to avoid startup skew.

ml-onboard-bot: updated configuration applied to quiet-burn run: rollout.policy.quiet_burn.min_n set, hysteresis=2, fallback=redwood-instruct-3b:fp16. storing failing examples to s3://onboard-debug/2208765432/failures (redacted).

leo: ok. capture this as runbook snippet and reconvene after next window. thanks all. :thumbsup:
